newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand blocks baht fund access through bourse.
newsitem.headline: Thailand blocks baht fund access through bourse.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Tuesday asked bank custodians and securities firms to help plug loopholes for foreigners to raise offshore baht after it denied currency speculators access to baht supply in mid-May.

The central bank, in a circular, asked bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and upaid securities sought by foreign investors. It said securities transfers could be made only for transactions with advance payment for stocks involved.
It said non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must be paid only in foreign currencies and the payment be made promptly to specific investors.
The central bank said the instruction was designed to prevent the Thai bourse from being used by currency dealers to gain access to baht funds for speculative purposes.

It said the Bank of Thailand would provide normal foreign exchange facilities for bona fide foreign investors in Thai stocks. It said foreigners wishing to sell Thai securities can freely repatriate foreign currencies out of Thailand.
The bank denied market talk that it was taking measures to halt foreign trading in Thai securities.
It said the authorities have no policy to disrupt activities at the bourse or impede efforts of offshore investors to repatriate foreign currency funds after selling Thai stocks.
